$comment: Every test-framework adapter, and the sample project that proves it is wired.
smoke.sh asserts this list covers every directory under examples/ — so a new port
that forgets to register itself fails the FIRST port's smoke run, not a code review.
command runs from the project directory via `sh -c`. It MUST defeat the build tool's
result cache: the smoke run changes only varar.lock.json, and a tool that decides
'nothing to do' from source timestamps reports a stale green and makes the whole
contract vacuous. That is why go carries -count=1 and gradle carries cleanTest.
gradle also carries --build-cache, which sounds backwards but is the point: cleanTest
defeats only the up-to-date check, so a build with the cache on (#84) restored a PASS
for a drifted baseline and the contract went vacuous exactly where it was loudest.
Running the samples WITH the cache keeps that path covered.
Every adapter reconciles varar.lock.json: it reads the baseline, gates on drift, and
rewrites it on a clean run. @varar/vitest was the last holdout — its plugin is a
build-time transform and must not write during one — until its reporter's end-of-run
hook took over the write, which is where every other port already does it.
probe.stalePath is the baseline-pruned probe: a path no docs glob matches (the
pre-varar/ location the samples actually migrated from, #70). Accepting drift must
drop it — removal is not gated, but dead state is not preserved either.

probe.name: You're really not going to like it
